welcome:
Welcome to the Nginx CLI Playground.
Type commands to explore a simulated production reverse proxy.
Type 'help' for available commands, 'scenario' for guided labs.

steps.instruction: First, check the installed Nginx version and compiled modules.
View the main Nginx configuration file to understand the current setup.
Now view the existing site configuration that we will modify for reverse proxy.
Check the upstream backend configuration for the Node.js app servers.
Test the configuration for syntax errors before reloading.
Reload Nginx to apply the new reverse proxy and TLS configuration.
Verify TLS is working by checking the certificate presented on port 443.
Test the reverse proxy end-to-end by sending an HTTP request through Nginx.
Users report 502 errors. Start by checking if Nginx itself is running.
Nginx is active. Check the error log for clues about the 502.
The error log shows 'connection refused' to upstream. Check the access log to confirm the pattern.
Verify which upstream backends are configured.
Test if the Node.js backend on port 3000 is actually responding.
Backend is down. Check the stub_status module to see current Nginx connection metrics.
Restart the Node.js backend (simulated), then test the proxy again.
Confirm the 502 is resolved by curling through the reverse proxy.

commands.help:
Available commands:
  nginx -t                        — Test configuration for syntax errors
  nginx -T                        — Test and dump full configuration
  nginx -s reload|stop|quit|reopen — Send signal to master process
  nginx -V                        — Show version and compiled modules
  nginx -v                        — Show version only
  cat <config file>               — View configuration files
  curl <url>                      — Test HTTP endpoints
  tail <log file>                 — View recent log entries
  systemctl status|restart nginx  — Manage Nginx service
  openssl s_client                — Test TLS certificates

  scenario                        — Start a guided lab
  clear                           — Clear the terminal
  help                            — Show this help

commands.cat /etc/nginx/conf.d/upstream.conf:
upstream nodejs_backend {
    least_conn;                        # route to server with fewest active connections
    server 127.0.0.1:3000 weight=3;   # primary backend (Node.js app)
    server 127.0.0.1:3001 weight=2;   # secondary backend
    server 127.0.0.1:3002 backup;     # only used when others are down
    keepalive 32;                      # persistent connections to backends
}
